boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Trinity destinations for studying, gathering, creating, and taking part in campus life.

cards.title: Set up at Coates Library
cards.subtitle: Library study and collaboration spaces
cards.notes: Use the library’s reader spaces for coursework, then reserve a study room when your group needs a defined place to work together.
cards.short_summary: A central academic space with study rooms, research support, and multiple campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes Coates Library as a campus living room where students collaborate, read, research, and study; it also houses the Writing Center and Tiger Learning Commons.
cards.source_title: Elizabeth Huth Coates Library | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Check current library building hours and room-reservation availability before visiting.

cards.title: Reserve a Coates study room
cards.subtitle: Inside Elizabeth Huth Coates Library
cards.notes: Book an individual or group room for a focused session, or use a walk-in room when one is available through the library’s process.
cards.short_summary: Sixteen reservable individual and group study rooms support planned work sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library Access Services states that sixteen individual and group study rooms are available, with walk-ins and online reservations.
cards.access_notes: Availability varies; reserve online or ask at the service desk.

cards.title: Bring a draft to Tiger Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Inside Coates Library
cards.notes: Pair a research or writing task with a visit to the commons, using its listed academic-support centers to move a project forward.
cards.short_summary: A named campus academic-support destination located within the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s campus directory lists Tiger Learning Commons under study and explore spaces, with the Quantitative Reasoning and Skills Center and Writing Center.
cards.source_title: Campus Buildings | Campus Directory | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Confirm individual center hours and appointment requirements before going.

cards.title: Meet up at Coates Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus gathering and student-services hub
cards.notes: Use the main entrance as a practical meetup point, then explore the center’s student-facing services, dining areas, and gathering spaces.
cards.short_summary: A central campus-life building with services and communal space.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies the Coates Student Center as a hub of campus life and says it facilitates discovery for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Building hours have special schedules and may change during the year.

cards.title: Use Skyline for a daytime meet-up
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Coates Student Center
cards.notes: Check whether Skyline is open before planning a meet-up; its multipurpose layout and second-floor location make it an easy named campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose second-floor room used as a weekday dining room.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity states that Skyline, including the Underwood Room, is a second-floor multi-purpose space used as a weekday dining room.
cards.access_notes: The space is open to the public but primarily used by Trinity faculty, staff, students, and guests; verify current access.

cards.title: Use Miller Fountain as a landmark
cards.subtitle: Trinity University campus
cards.notes: Choose the fountain as a clear outdoor rendezvous point before heading to an event or another campus destination, and keep pathways unobstructed.
cards.short_summary: A named 1966 Trinity fountain with a documented campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the Eugenia B. Miller Fountain was presented to the University in 1966 and named for Eugenia B. Miller.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access can be affected by weather or campus event setup.

cards.title: Catch a recital at Ruth Taylor
cards.subtitle: Smith Music Building, Ruth Taylor Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Look for the music department’s public concert listings and arrive a little early; the hall is a specific place to experience student and guest performances.
cards.short_summary: A recital venue within Trinity’s fine-arts complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies the Campbell and Eloise Smith Music Building as home to the Ruth Taylor Recital Hall, and its music ensembles rehearse there.
cards.source_title: Ruth Taylor Fine Arts Center | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: The fine-arts center lists hours of Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–10 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m.–6 p.m., and Sunday noon–10 p.m.; event access may differ.

cards.title: Move through the Bell Center
cards.subtitle: Athletics and fitness complex
cards.notes: Bring your Trinity ID if eligible and use the complex for fitness or to orient yourself before a game, practice, or other athletic activity.
cards.short_summary: The core of Trinity’s athletic complex, with gyms, fitness facilities, and a natatorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes the William H. Bell Center as the core of its athletic complex and says it contains performance gyms, Hixon Natatorium, and fitness facilities.
cards.source_title: William H. Bell Center | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: The facility is available to Trinity students, faculty, and staff with Trinity ID; special hours may change.

cards.title: Find a club or intramural game
cards.subtitle: Outdoor recreation field near Bell Center
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule, then watch or join an appropriately organized activity rather than entering a field that is already reserved for play.
cards.short_summary: A turf field used for club-sport practices, competitions, and intramurals.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity states that Jim Potter Intramural Field hosts club-sport practices and competitions as well as intramural competition.
cards.source_title: William H. Bell Center | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Use only when open or scheduled; follow university recreation and facility rules.

cards.title: Attend a Parker Chapel program
cards.subtitle: Campus chapel and event venue
cards.notes: Review the university calendar for an appropriate public program, then use the chapel as a named campus setting for reflection, music, or community events.
cards.short_summary: A listed campus gathering place that also hosts Trinity’s Vespers tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s campus directory lists Parker Chapel among campus gathering places, and the Music Department identifies Trinity Vespers at Parker Chapel as a candlelit lesson-and-carols service.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled programs and chapel operations; consult the campus calendar.
